glossary.Ask: A resting offer to sell. Best ask is the lowest visible selling price.
glossary.Bid: A resting offer to buy. Best bid is the highest visible buying price.
glossary.Limit order: Buy no higher, or sell no lower, than your limit. The remainder queues.
glossary.Market order: Trade now against available opposite orders. Unfilled remainder cancels.
glossary.Mid: Halfway between best bid and ask. Nobody promises to trade there.
glossary.P&L: Profit and loss from opening equity. The public mark values unsold inventory.
glossary.Partial fill: Only some requested units traded. A limit remainder may keep waiting.
glossary.Position: Units owned: positive is long, negative is short. Buys add; sells subtract.
glossary.Spread: Best ask minus best bid. It is a price gap, not guaranteed profit.
glossary.VWAP: Sum of each fill's price × quantity, divided by total filled units.

layers.interview: What is the delta exposure of short 10 contracts with delta 0.60 and multiplier 100?
layers.intuition: The multiplier specifies how many underlying units each option contract represents. Quantity and multiplier are separate.
layers.maths: Position Greek = signed contracts × multiplier × per-underlying-unit Greek. In this recorded example, the calculation gives 51.14357531.

layers.interview: Why can more frequent hedging reduce exposure yet increase costs?
layers.intuition: Hedging is an actual trade. Whole units, bid/ask, depth and future changes prevent perfect continuous replication.
layers.maths: Option exposure = sum(q_j × m_j × delta_j); target stock = minus that exposure, rounded to whole units. q_j is signed contracts and m_j multiplier. In this recorded example, the calculation gives -51.00000000.

layers.interview: Explain how cash can rise while marked P&L falls.
layers.intuition: Premium buys an option asset. Its marked value, subsequent gains or losses and fees determine P&L; paying cash is not itself the same as losing it.
layers.maths: Cash flow = −q × m × p; q is signed contracts, m multiplier, p execution premium per underlying unit. Fees are separate. In this recorded example, the calculation gives -230.21510000.
